content: Norfloxacin is a synthetic, broad-spectrum antibacterial agent designed for oral administration. It belongs to the fluoroquinolone class of antibiotics and is chemically identified as 1-ethyl-6-fluoro-1,4-dihydro-4-oxo-7-(1-piperazinyl)-3-quinolinecarboxylic acid. The compound has a melting point of approximately 221°C. Norfloxacin is freely soluble in glacial acetic acid but exhibits very slight solubility in ethanol, methanol, and water. It is commercially available in 400-mg tablets. Each tablet contains the following inactive ingredients: cellulose, croscarmellose sodium, hydroxypropyl cellulose, hydroxypropyl methylcellulose, magnesium stearate, and titanium dioxide. As a fluoroquinolone, norfloxacin is structurally distinct from non-fluorinated quinolones due to the presence of a fluorine atom at the 6th position and a piperazine moiety at the 7th position of its molecular structure.
